tasks.title: Task 1
tasks.instructions: Read the passage, then read again and choose the correct answers. Questions 39-42: /4x1=4 points/; questions 43-44: /2x3=6 points/
tasks.text:
(1) Why do some people find it easy to go for a run every morning, while others give up after a week? The answer may have less to do with willpower than we think. Psychologists say that much of what we do each day is not the result of decisions at all, but of habits.

(2) A habit is an action that has become automatic. Researchers describe it as a loop with three parts: a cue, such as waking up or arriving home; a routine, which is the action itself; and a reward, the good feeling that follows. Each time the loop is repeated, the link between the cue and the action becomes stronger.

(3) How long does it take to build a new habit? A popular claim says twenty-one days, but research suggests otherwise. In a well-known study at University College London, volunteers chose a simple daily action, such as drinking a glass of water after breakfast. On average it took about sixty-six days before the action felt automatic, and for some people it took much longer.

(4) The same study found that missing a single day did not really matter. What mattered was coming back to the habit the next day. People who gave up after one mistake rarely succeeded, while those who simply continued usually did.

(5) Experts therefore suggest starting small. Instead of promising to run five kilometres every day, a beginner might promise to put on running shoes after breakfast. Linking the new action to an existing habit also helps, for example reading for ten minutes straight after brushing your teeth in the evening.

(6) So, is willpower useless? Not completely. But perhaps it is better used to design a good routine than to fight against bad habits every day. The person who runs every morning may not be stronger than everyone else; he or she may simply have made running easier to start.

questions.stem: What is the topic of the passage?
What does "a cue" mean in paragraph 2?

options.B: the thing that starts the action

options.B: Missing one day usually ruins a new habit.
options.C: Habits always form in exactly twenty-one days.
options.E: All habits are bad for us.

questions.stem: Which people are most likely to succeed in building a habit? People who ___.

questions.stem: According to the study at University College London, what did the volunteers do?

options.A: They ran five kilometres every day.
options.D: They chose a simple daily action and repeated it.
options.E: They tested their willpower in a laboratory.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the author's opinion?

options.B: Only strong people can form habits.
options.C: Running every morning is impossible for most people.
options.D: Designing a good routine is more useful than relying on willpower alone.
